title: Graded Nakayama generation
statement: Let k be a field and S=k[x_0,x_1] with total-degree grading S_d equal to the k-span of monomials of degree d and S_d=0 for d<0 [def-sc-p1-standard]. Let S_+=(x_0,x_1). If N is a finitely generated Z-graded S-module and homogeneous elements n_1,...,n_r have images generating N/S_+N as a k-vector space, then n_1,...,n_r generate N as an S-module. In particular, if N/S_+N=0, then N=0.

source.place: proof, graded Nakayama criterion applied to K_2

proof.text: Choose B such that N_j=0 for j<B using [lem-sc-p1-finite-graded-module-lower-bound]. Work in N itself with Q the polynomial span of the given homogeneous lifts, avoiding the construction of a quotient grading.

source.place: proof: graded Hilbert syzygy theorem; standard graded Nakayama argument expanded in lem-sc-p1-graded-nakayama-generation, not explicit in the blueprint

proof.text: Prove by induction on a∈ℕ that every x∈N_j with j<B+a belongs to Q. The base case has x=0. In the successor case [lem-sc-p1-graded-quotient-span-descent] writes x=q+x_0y+x_1z, where q∈Q and y,z have degree j-1<B+a. The induction hypothesis and scalar/additive closure of Q give x∈Q.

source.place: proof: graded Hilbert syzygy theorem; standard graded Nakayama argument expanded in lem-sc-p1-graded-nakayama-generation, not explicit in the blueprint

proof.text: For a homogeneous element of degree j use a=max(j-B,0)+1 in the induction. Every element is a finite sum of homogeneous elements by the internal direct sum, so Q=N.

source.place: proof: graded Hilbert syzygy theorem; standard graded Nakayama argument expanded in lem-sc-p1-graded-nakayama-generation, not explicit in the blueprint

proof.text: For the vanishing corollary restrict the scalar action along k→S to install a compatible k-module structure. Apply the generation theorem with r=0: the quotient span condition holds because the quotient is subsingleton. The empty polynomial span is bottom, hence bottom=top and every element of N is zero.
